To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) The uptake, distribution and solvation of fluorescent molecules in 3D spheroids differ from that in 2D cell cultures; and 2) The covalent dye CPM exhibits intermittent oscillations of fluorescence intensity in 3D tumor spheroids.
the spectral properties of fluorescent dyes are significantly altered by the 3D environment.
(a) the total uptake of a non-covalently interacting anti-cancer drug is significantly lower in the 3 D tumor cell as compared to the 2 D cell.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of 3D tumor spheroids using time-resolved confcal microscopy.
the development of new optical methods and instrumentation to probe 3D tumor cells.
understanding the behavior of small molecules in 3D tumor-like spheroids.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 3D multi cellular tumor spheroid is a very complex system.
the spectral properties of a 3D tumor spheroid differ significantly from a 2-D cell.
2D cell cultures are not representative of the 3D cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
3D cells are different from 2D cells in many aspects and this difference is reflected in the spectral mapping of the 3D cells.
3D tumor cells are different from 2D cells, and this difference may be exploited to design novel anti-cancer drugs.
3D tumors are significantly different from the 2D cells, and the difference is not only in the morphology but also in the dynamics and function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a 3D tumor is not just a stack of 2D cells, and hence, it should not be treated as such.
3D tumor cells are very different from their 2D counterparts.
the 3D multi cellular spheroids are not the same as 2D cells and hence cannot be considered as a model for 2D cells.
